sources.quote: Hartree, who had recently moved from Manchester to Cambridge to take up his Plummer Chair of Mathematical Physics at the Cavendish Laboratory...
Hartree would soon become a member of the NPL Executive Committee.
Perhaps his most famous scientific contribution is his insight into how to solve the Schrödinger equation for a multielectron atom using a self-consistent field approximation scheme [25].

note: Disputed the meaning of digital computers.

sources.quote: In the postwar years, these questions were debated by Alan Turing and Douglas Hartree, who differed in their interpretations of the digital computer as a new piece of science and technology.

note: Mobilized Lovelace's notes in his arguments.

sources.quote: This statement is quoted by Hartree [15, p. 70] who adds: 'This does not imply that it may not be possible to construct electronic equipment which will "think for itself,"...'
